content.text: Investigation complete: §21.1–21.4 is the only liability-limitation language in the document (no competing cap in the warranty, insurance or general sections; §18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities). The clause meets the **preferred** checklist in full, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Section 21 sits at our preferred position and needs no change. The cap in 21.1 is expressly mutual ("each Party's total aggregate liability... The cap is mutual") and is set at the greater of Fees paid or payable by Customer in the trailing twelve months and USD 1,000,000. "Fees" (1.5) captures recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the fee-based limb is substantive rather than illusory (the only minor gap is that a one-time implementation charge is excluded unless an Order Form says otherwise, and the USD 1,000,000 floor plus the USD 2,000,000 annual commitment in 2.1 make that immaterial). Section 21.2 excludes indirect and consequential damages mutually ("neither Party is liable"), while preserving data-restoration, replacement-service, notice and incident-response costs as direct damages — a customer-favourable addition. Section 21.3 places outside the cap, for either Party, breach of confidentiality, data-protection or security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's IP, i.e. all preferred carve-outs. The final sentence of 21.3 confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services "is not damages and is not limited by this Section"; read with 21.1 this is the standard payment carve-out from the damages cap and does not create any uncapped Customer liability exposure beyond paying for conforming Services. Section 21.4 preserves the independence and survival of each cap. No walk-away trigger is present: Customer is not uncapped, the Vendor cap is well above six months' fees, and indemnities sit outside the cap.
